## PDF page 156

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=156)

```text
                              CHAPTER THIRTEEN



                       OPEN-RAISING


Now it is time to get into the preflop-specific section of this workbook. Up to
this point, the exercises have largely been focused on the math of the game.
These upcoming chapters aim to bridge the math with preflop spots to help
you look at preflop from a more technical point of view.

To begin, we will focus on open-raising situations. An open-raise is when
the first person to enter the pot preflop does so by raising. This also includes
steals, which are specific open-raises from the CO, BTN, and SB.

TOOLS TO USE: Any range software (Flopzilla, Equilab, PokerCruncher, etc.)
and a calculator will work.

PROCESS: Each page contains a preflop open-raising exercise where action
folds around to you in the SB. Start by getting the %-form for the range you
assume the BB would defend with (defending includes both calls and 3bets).
Then, answer the questions below.

TAKEAWAYS: Most players only use a single raise in this preflop spot, so notice
the difference between the BB’s defense range when the size changes. Are
there spots in your game where a larger size could create more folds and
allow you to steal the blinds more aggressively?

GLGL.


                                   PA G E 1 5 6
```

## PDF page 160

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=160)

```text
              BUTTON OPEN-RAISING


Now you will look at spots where you are on the button.

Action folds around to you and you have two players left to act, the SB and
BB. You are given the defense range for each player, and will start by filling
out the %-form for both.

Then answer the questions below. Remember that you can find how often
everyone will fold by multiplying every player’s folding frequency together. If
the SB defends with 20% of hands and the BB defends with 30% of hands, that
means they fold 80% and 70% of the time respectively. 80%*70% = 56% chance
that both players fold when your raise. Feel free to do this by hand, or use my
“Multiple Folders” spreadsheet available at www.splitsuit.pro/sheets

Keep in mind that the defense ranges are slightly simplified, since the BB
may very well defend differently if the SB calls or folds. On the other hand,
the SB may 3bet differently with the BB still to act. Static defense ranges are
given here to make your exploration easier, but real-world ranges can be
more fluid.

Once again, pay attention and compare the outright success rate of both
raise sizes. Using a larger raise size does require more folds to find an auto-
profit steal, but finding auto-profit steals can easily improve your winrate.

GLGL.


                                   PA G E 1 6 0
```
